Subject: Re: Tailored exclusion language for SaaS Order Form — bridge language proposal

Kimberly / Marissa —

Thanks for the redline. Two points from Acme Legal:

1) Punitive and special damages: we generally do not accept a broad one-way exclusion that would prevent recovery for third-party regulatory fines or punitive damages where Redwood's conduct is egregious (e.g., willful breach or gross negligence). We need carve-outs for (a) claims arising from Redwood's intentional misconduct, and (b) third-party regulatory penalties directly caused by Redwood.

2) Consequential vs. incidental: the current draft lumps "consequential, special, incidental, punitive or exemplary" together with a mutual exclusion. Acme requests either (i) a mutual exclusion with a written, enumerated list of exclusions (lost profits, loss of business, loss of data), or (ii) if you insist on one-way language, keep exceptions for third-party claims and regulatory costs.

Attached are our annotated comments on the order form. Please confirm whether your position is to keep the exclusion mutual, and if so, whether you can accept narrower exceptions tied to fraud/intentionally wrongful acts and regulatory fines.

Regards,

Claire D'Souza
Senior Counsel, Acme Cloud
Acme Cloud Services

Subject: Re: Tailored exclusion language for SaaS Order Form — bridge language proposal

Claire —

Appreciate the clear note and the annotated PDF. Quick high-level: Redwood's standard position has been a mutual exclusion of consequential/special/incidental/punitive/exemplary damages, with limited carve-outs for (i) willful misconduct/intentional wrongdoing and (ii) liability that cannot legally be excluded. We try to avoid broad carve-outs for regulatory fines because that can be extremely high and effectively negate the economic cap. That said, we want a path to close. Proposed path forward:

- Suggested compromise language (see attached text file): maintain a mutual exclusion but explicitly carve out: 
  a) damages resulting from Redwood's fraud, willful misconduct, or intentional breach;
  b) statutory fines/penalties only to the extent they are third-party claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct (narrowly drafted);
  c) the exclusion does not apply to the Parties' obligations under the indemnity for IP infringement or the payment obligations in the Order Form.

- Add a short definition section for "Consequential Damages" that lists typical examples (lost profits, lost business, loss of data) so the parties have predictable scope rather than litigating labels.

Would you be open to trialing that bridge language? If Acme accepts the proposed exceptions narrowly tied to willful misconduct/gross negligence and statutory obligations that cannot be excluded, we can preserve the cap and mutuality while addressing your legal team's concerns.

Attaching: proposed-exclusion-text-20260915.txt (txt) and a redline of the Order Form (ACME_OrderForm_redline_v3.docx).

Best,

Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Contracts (Sales)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Tailored exclusion language for SaaS Order Form — bridge language proposal

Kimberly —

Thanks for the counterproposal and the concrete draft. The enumerated examples help. Two follow-ups from Acme Legal after internal review:

1) The carve-out for statutory fines/penalties is still too broad as drafted. We can accept a narrow gross-negligence/willful-misconduct qualifier, but we need the exposure to be limited to direct regulatory penalties assessed against Redwood (not downstream consequential business losses caused by a regulator's action).

2) We need clarity on interaction with the indemnity. Specifically: if Acme is sued by a customer because of data exposure traceable to Redwood, will Redwood's indemnity cover third-party claims and defense costs even if consequential damages are excluded? Acme wants the indemnity to operate independently of the damages exclusion (i.e., indemnity survives and covers third-party claims arising from Redwood's breach of security obligations).

If Redwood agrees to the narrow statutory carve-out language and confirms indemnity independence for third-party security claims, Acme Legal is willing to move to clean order form redlines.

Regards,

Claire

Subject: Re: Tailored exclusion language for SaaS Order Form — bridge language proposal

Claire —

Thank you — this is helpful and close. We talked to Legal (Markus looped here) and propose the final compromise language below; happy to insert into the Order Form redline for quick sign-off. High-level: mutual exclusion preserved; carve-outs narrowly focused on Redwood's intentional or grossly negligent conduct and an indemnity carve that preserves third-party defense & indemnity for security/data claims. Draft: 

"Neither Party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, incidental, punitive or exemplary damages, including, without limitation, lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, loss of use, or loss of customers, except as follows: (a) for damages arising from a Party's fraud, willful misconduct or gross negligence; (b) statutory fines or monetary penalties levied by a governmental authority that are the direct result of Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence, but in no event shall such fines include consequential economic losses of the other Party resulting from the imposition of such fines; and (c) nothing in this Section limits either Party's obligations under any indemnity set forth in this Agreement, including indemnities that cover third-party claims arising from a Party's breach of its security obligations."

Please confirm if Acme is comfortable with this exact wording and we'll push a clean redline to Tom for procurement.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
